Sid,  

I am writing this from my bed; my old joints are warmed by blankets and a proper hearthfire. It took all of my vim to shoo the family from my room to have some peace and quiet just to write this. They fuss and fuss over my health, but they're wound up over nothing, and it does no good to worry the great-grandchildren. Besides, we could all be gobbled up by one of those massive dragon beasties any day, should one of them fix their attention our way.  

I hear mumbles, you know, that tell of creatures of fire and stone in far-off depths, places even unknown to the families of Clan Way. Us Waylits are a resourceful bunch, though, and the council of clans won't let this go ignored, not for long. Trials for the younger generations, I guess, not an old bat like me. I reckon you'll have a laugh at me calling myself "old" and to that I say, "Be nice," or I'll see that my spark haunts you for all of time.  

Truth be told, I worry about you. You carry much in your many arms and trust so few to help bear those burdens. It's not my place to dote on you or suggest advice; heck, in contrast, I've been but a passing moment in your absurdly long life. Even so, it is my singular hope that I helped illuminate your way in that fleeting moment. The lantern at your hilt.  

—Gruna

_Page One_  
  
Rhea is dead. The twins care more about the killing than the purpose. This place was a beacon for five minutes, until it turned into a house of flagellantism.  
  
All of Gavril's citizens are gone now. A few managed to escape, but most of them died on the bloodstone. I don't even remember when the last one was killed... A year ago now? Two? We've been killing each other for so long, I can hardly separate killing for survival over killing for the ritual...  
  
What happened here? One day, we were following Saul's vision in pursuit of the golden city, and now I can't sleep without fear. Surely I lifted a brow when he said that he found such a city  tucked in the isles—even without proof, I stayed loyal. I followed. But when he asked us to stay behind on the order of the Unseen Ones...

strings.en:
_An Unofficial History of the Wizard's Court, Volume 2_    
  
by A. Hawthorn (signed 716 AE)    
  
The more dead ends I encounter while attempting to piece together a meaningful timeline of the foundation of the Wizard's Court to present, the more I realize: a history of the court would simply be a history of Isgarren himself.  
  
I am at least a little excited to venture down this path, as I've spent my entire time in the Astral Ward focusing on watching the continued escalation in Elona (for which Isgarren has shown little interest, which shocks me given his "impassioned" hatred for the demonic).  
  
In the absence of (attainable) records, I've decided to gather information on the curator by posing a question to the other chairs. Mabon, Waiting Sorrow, and Dagda—two of whom were most definitely from the same era as Isgarren himself, being from the "elder races" of Tyria.  
  
I spoke with Mabon first, given that he spends a great deal of time holed up in the private reading rooms of the library. He seemed bemused when I told him of Isgarren's little assignment. Shocked, even, but offered little beyond what we all already know: that Mabon was Isgarren's first "recruit."  
  
Mabon paused for a few moments, reflecting on that time. He noted the war between the seers and the mursaat. Isgarren "spared him," supposedly, and for that Mabon will always be in his debt. He didn't say much else of note. He was quiet, and I expected him to be.
